mainTopic: The end of פרק כל הזבחים on when carrying the blood counts as a real עבודה, and the start of the next פרק on people who disqualify a קרבן by collecting its blood, beginning with the source for a זר.
overview: The amud opens with the end of רב ירמיה מדיפתי's reasoning: the blood still has to be brought to the מזבח again. רבי ירמיה tells רב אשי that this idea depends on a מחלוקת between רבי אליעזר and the רבנן about 'needed' carrying of the blood. רבא explains that everyone agrees carrying toward the מזבח is needed and carrying away from it is not. The two sides argue only about bringing the blood back in a second time. אביי challenges this from a ברייתא in רבי אליעזר's name, and רבא accepts it ('אי תניא, תניא'). The first פרק then ends with a הדרן. The second פרק opens with a משנה listing people whose collecting of the blood disqualifies a קרבן, such as a זר, a טמא, or one who collects with the left hand, where רבי שמעון disagrees. The גמרא looks for the source that a זר disqualifies. It reads a פסוק in a new way, then starts a קל וחומר from a בעל מום that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The blood still has to be brought again
steps.stepSummary: The closing word of רב ירמיה מדיפתי's explanation: because the blood must be carried to the מזבח again, that second carrying is a real part of the service.
steps.simpleTranslation: [...since it is necessary] to bring it [again].
steps.whatsHappening: This single word finishes a sentence that began earlier. רב ירמיה מדיפתי's point is that the blood still needs to be brought to the מזבח again.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because the blood has to be carried over again, the second carrying is not extra. It counts as a real הולכה, so it must be done properly by a כהן.

keyTerms.meaning: to bring it (here, to carry the blood to the מזבח)
carrying the blood to the מזבח, one of the four main blood services

steps.confusionAlert: This word is the end of a sentence from the previous lines, not a new statement. The full phrase is 'הא צריך לאמטוייה' (it still needs to be brought), and it is quoted in full in the next step.

phrases.english: to bring it [again].

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רב ירמיה מדיפתי's reasoning from the previous section.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Logical reason: the second carrying is still needed
steps.terutzMaskana: The second carrying to the מזבח counts as a real עבודה because the blood must still get there.

steps.title: This reasoning depends on a מחלוקת
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה tells רב אשי that רב ירמיה מדיפתי's reasoning ('it needs to be brought again') depends on the מחלוקת between רבי אליעזר and the רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה said to רב אשי: This is what רב ירמיה מדיפתי said. The idea 'it still needs to be brought' depends on the disagreement between רבי אליעזר and the רבנן.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה reports that רב ירמיה מדיפתי himself tied his reasoning to an existing מחלוקת. The reasoning is not agreed on by everyone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before this, the idea that 'needed carrying counts' looked like a simple rule. Now we learn it follows only one side of a known disagreement. The next step brings the source of that disagreement.

keyTerms.meaning: this is what he said (reporting someone's exact words)

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה לְרַב אָשֵׁי,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya said to Rav Ashi:
This is what Rav Yirmeya of Difti said:
"It still needs to be brought" —
is the disagreement of Rabbi Eliezer and the Rabbis.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that the reasoning from step 1 depends on a known מחלוקת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The idea that 'needed carrying' counts as a real עבודה follows one side of the מחלוקת between רבי אליעזר and the רבנן.

steps.title: The משנה where רבי אליעזר splits needed and unneeded carrying
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה: for רבי אליעזר, bad intent while carrying disqualifies only when the carrying is needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a משנה: רבי אליעזר says, if someone carries the blood where carrying is needed, bad intent disqualifies the קרבן. Where carrying is not needed, bad intent does not disqualify.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the source of the מחלוקת mentioned in step 2. It is רבי אליעזר's teaching in the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי אליעזר, only carrying that is truly needed counts as a real עבודה, so only then can a wrong מחשבה ruin the קרבן. The next steps show where the רבנן actually differ from him.

keyTerms.meaning: wrong intent (like פיגול) disqualifies the קרבן
one who walks or carries (the blood)

steps.whyThisMatters: This needed/unneeded split decides when a carrying is a real עבודה. That affects both bad intent and who is allowed to do the carrying.

phrases.english: As we learned: Rabbi Eliezer says:
One who carries where he needs to carry —
intent disqualifies.
Where he does not need to carry —
intent does not disqualify.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Quotes the source of the מחלוקת named in step 2.
steps.raayaObject: That a מחלוקת exists about whether only needed carrying counts as a real עבודה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה with רבי אליעזר's view on needed and unneeded carrying.

steps.title: רבא defines needed and unneeded carrying
steps.stepSummary: רבא says everyone agrees: carrying toward the מזבח is needed, and carrying away from it is not.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבא said: Everyone agrees that if he received the blood far away and brought it close, that is needed carrying. If he received it close and took it away, that is unneeded carrying.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא explains the two terms from רבי אליעזר's משנה. This prepares for the next step of the discussion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Outside' means far from the מזבח and 'inside' means close to it. Carrying toward the מזבח moves the service forward, so it is needed. Carrying away from it is not. Both sides agree on these two cases, and the next step shows the one case they do argue about.

keyTerms.meaning: he received it (the blood, in a כלי)
far from the מזבח / close to the מזבח

steps.whatToRemember: Toward the מזבח = needed carrying. Away from the מזבח = unneeded carrying. רבי אליעזר holds that only needed carrying is a real עבודה.
steps.confusionAlert: Here 'outside' and 'inside' do not mean outside or inside the עזרה. They mean far from or close to the מזבח.

phrases.english: And Rava said: All agree:
if he received it outside and brought it inside —
phrases.notes: 'Outside' means far from the מזבח, and 'inside' means close to it.

phrases.english: that is carrying that is needed.
If he received it inside and took it outside —
that is carrying that is not needed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defines the key terms of the משנה quoted in step 3, setting up the discussion that follows.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Carrying toward the מזבח is needed carrying, and carrying away from the מזבח is unneeded carrying. All agree on these definitions.

steps.title: רבא pinpoints the only case of disagreement
steps.stepSummary: רבא says the argument is only about blood that was brought in, taken out, and must now be brought in again. The רבנן count that trip as needed, and רבי אליעזר does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: They argue only where he brought the blood in and then took it out again. One Sage (the תנא קמא) holds: it still has to be brought to the מזבח, so that trip counts. The other Sage (רבי אליעזר) holds: it is not like carrying that the service needs.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא continues his statement from the last step. He shows exactly which case the two sides argue about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Carrying toward the מזבח counts, and carrying away does not. That much is agreed. The open question is a 'repeat' trip: the blood already reached the מזבח once, was taken away, and now must come back. The רבנן say that return trip is a real part of the service. רבי אליעזר says it is not, because the needed carrying already happened.

phrases.english: They disagree only
where he brought it in and took it out again;
one Sage holds: it still needs to be brought (to the altar),
phrases.notes: This is the תנא קמא (the רבנן).

phrases.english: and the other Sage holds:
it is not like carrying that is needed for the service.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא נֶחְלְקוּ אֶלָּא כְּשֶׁהִכְנִיסוֹ וְחָזַר וְהוֹצִיאוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רבא's statement from step 4. After saying what everyone agrees on, he names the one case they argue about.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The מחלוקת is only about bringing the blood back in a second time. The רבנן count it as needed carrying, and רבי אליעזר does not.

steps.title: אביי challenges רבא from a ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: אביי quotes a ברייתא in which רבי אליעזר says carrying from outside to inside is needed carrying. That should include bringing the blood back in a second time.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי objected: רבי אליעזר says, if someone carries the blood where it needs to be carried, bad intent disqualifies. How so? If he collected it outside and brought it inside, that is needed carrying. If he collected it inside and took it outside, that is carrying that is not needed. So if he brought it back in again, that is needed carrying!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי attacks רבא's claim that רבי אליעזר does not count the return trip. He uses a ברייתא in רבי אליעזר's own name.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא gives a simple test in the name of רבי אליעזר. Moving toward the מזבח (outside to inside) is needed, and moving away is not. By that test, bringing the blood back inward is also moving toward the מזבח, so it should be needed carrying. If so, רבי אליעזר agrees with the רבנן, and רבא's picture of the argument falls apart.

keyTerms.meaning: Far from the מזבח / near the מזבח

phrases.english: Abaye raised an objection to him (Rava):
Rabbi Eliezer says:
one who carries (the blood) where he needs to carry it –
(bad) intent disqualifies.
How so?
If he collected it outside and brought it inside –
phrases.notes: 'Outside' means farther from the מזבח, and 'inside' means closer to it.

phrases.english: that is carrying that needs to be done.
If he collected it inside and took it outside –
that is carrying that does not need to be done.
So if he went back and brought it in again –
it is carrying that needs to be done!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבא's claim in step 5 that רבי אליעזר does not count the second inward trip.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's claim that רבי אליעזר does not count bringing the blood back in as needed carrying.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי אליעזר's own ברייתא says any carrying from outside to inside is needed. The return trip is outside to inside, so רבי אליעזר must count it.

steps.title: רבא accepts the ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers: if this ברייתא is really taught, then it is taught. He accepts it and does not argue.
steps.simpleTranslation: He (רבא) said to him: If it is taught, it is taught.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives up his position. He admits that a ברייתא outranks his own explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא does not try to answer the challenge. If the ברייתא is a real source, it settles the matter. So רבא's explanation of where רבי אליעזר and the רבנן argue is set aside.

keyTerms.meaning: If it was taught, it was taught. In other words: I accept it and cannot argue.

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a clever answer that saves רבא's view. It is a concession: רבא accepts the ברייתא and drops his explanation.

phrases.english: He (Rava) said to him:
If it is taught, it is taught.
phrases.notes: He means: if this ברייתא is real, I can't argue with it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to אביי's challenge in step 6 by giving in.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The ברייתא stands: רבי אליעזר also counts carrying the blood inward as needed. רבא's explanation is set aside.

steps.title: Hadran — Closing פרק כל הזבחים
steps.stepSummary: The closing formula for the first פרק of מסכת זבחים, כל הזבחים.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, כל הזבחים.
steps.whatsHappening: This line marks the end of the first פרק. It is not part of the argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The הדרן is a traditional goodbye to the פרק we just finished, with a promise to come back and learn it again. The next פרק starts with a new משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: We will return to you (said when finishing a פרק)
The name of the first פרק of זבחים

steps.whatToRemember: פרק כל הזבחים ends with the question of when carrying the blood counts as part of the service. Carrying toward the מזבח counts, and carrying away does not. After אביי's ברייתא, רבא accepts that רבי אליעזר also counts bringing the blood back in a second time as needed carrying.

phrases.english: We will return to you, "All slaughtered offerings"

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the פרק after the end of the sugya in step 7.

steps.title: New פרק: the list of people whose blood-collecting disqualifies
steps.stepSummary: The משנה lists people who ruin a קרבן if they collect its blood: a זר, an אונן, a טבול יום, a מחוסר כפורים, a מחוסר בגדים, one who did not wash hands and feet, an ערל, a טמא, one sitting, and one standing on something.
steps.simpleTranslation: If any of these collected the blood of a קרבן, the קרבן is disqualified: a non-כהן, a mourner on the day of death, someone who toveled today, someone still missing his atonement קרבן, a כהן without his special clothes, a כהן who did not wash hands and feet, an uncircumcised כהן, an impure כהן, a כהן who was sitting, or a כהן standing on vessels, on an animal, or on his friend's feet.
steps.whatsHappening: A new פרק begins with a new משנה. It gives a long list of people who are not fit to collect the blood, and it says their collecting makes the קרבן פסול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: קבלת הדם is one of the main עבודות of a קרבן, so it must be done by a fit כהן in the proper way. The list mixes two kinds of problems: the person himself is not fit (זר, טמא, אונן), or the way he serves is wrong (sitting, or standing on something between him and the floor of the עזרה).

keyTerms.meaning: A mourner on the day a close relative died, before the burial
Someone who toveled today and must wait for nightfall to be fully טהור
Someone who still has to bring his atonement קרבן (like a זב or a מצורע)

phrases.english: MISHNA: All offerings whose blood was collected by
a non-priest, an acute mourner, one who immersed that day,
one lacking atonement, or one lacking the priestly garments,
one who did not wash hands and feet,
an uncircumcised one, an impure one, one who is sitting,
phrases.notes: The ערל here is a כהן whose ברית was held back for a medical reason.

phrases.english: one standing on top of vessels,

phrases.aramaic: עַל גַּבֵּי בְּהֵמָה, עַל גַּבֵּי רַגְלֵי חֲבֵרוֹ – פָּסַל.
phrases.english: on top of an animal, or on top of his friend's feet — he disqualified it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the second פרק right after the הדרן in step 8.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If any of the listed unfit people collect the blood, the קרבן is פסול.

steps.title: Collecting with the left hand: a dispute
steps.stepSummary: Collecting the blood with the left hand disqualifies, but רבי שמעון holds it is כשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he collected the blood with his left hand, he disqualified it. רבי שמעון says it is fit.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds one more case, collecting with the left hand, and here there is an argument. The תנא קמא says it is פסול, and רבי שמעון says it is כשר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unlike the list before it, which is stated with no dispute, this case has a named disagreement. רבי שמעון does not count left-handed collecting as a disqualifying flaw.

phrases.english: If he collected with the left hand — he disqualified it.
Rabbi Shimon deems it fit.

steps.triggerLanguage: קִבֵּל בִּשְׂמֹאל – פָּסַל. רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן מַכְשִׁיר.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a final, disputed case to the משנה's list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: תנא קמא: collecting with the left hand is פסול. רבי שמעון: it is כשר.

steps.title: Source for a non-priest disqualifying
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens by asking for the source that a זר disqualifies the עבודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know that a non-כהן disqualifies?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts with the first item on the משנה's list, the זר, and asks for its source in the תורה. This sets up the next move.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is not whether a זר may serve. It is where we learn that his serving actually ruins the קרבן.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know it?

phrases.english: GEMARA: A non-priest — from where do we derive it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the גמרא's discussion of the first case in the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The פסוק that teaches a זר's עבודה disqualifies the קרבן.

steps.title: לוי quotes the verse about separating from the holy items
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers with a ברייתא of לוי, which quotes ויקרא 22:2: "Speak to אהרן and his sons, that they separate from the holy things of בני ישראל."
steps.simpleTranslation: As לוי taught: "Speak to אהרן and to his sons, that they keep away from the holy things of the children of Israel..."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings לוי's teaching, which points to a פסוק in ויקרא. This begins the answer, but the גמרא first has to work out how this פסוק teaches about a זר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At first glance the פסוק talks to כהנים about keeping away from קדשים when they are טמא. It does not seem to be about a זר at all. The words "בני ישראל" will be the key to the derivation.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't expect the זר source to be obvious from this פסוק. As it reads simply, it is about impure כהנים. The גמרא will soon read it in a new way to get to a זר.

phrases.english: As Levi teaches:
"Speak to Aaron and to his sons, saying,
that they separate themselves from the holy things of the children of Israel, etc." —

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts to answer the question of step 11 by bringing a פסוק through לוי's ברייתא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The source is ויקרא 22:2, as taught by לוי. How it teaches about a זר is worked out in the following steps.

steps.title: What do the words "children of Israel" come to exclude?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what "בני ישראל" leaves out, since it seems to limit the law to the קדשים of בני ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: "The children of Israel" — what does it come to leave out?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא focuses on the words "בני ישראל." Read simply, they suggest that only the קדשים of בני ישראל are covered, and so some other group's קרבנות are not. It asks who that group would be.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the rule of keeping away in טומאה applies only to the קדשים "of בני ישראל," then someone else's קרבן could be brought in טומאה. The גמרא now tests which group that could be.

phrases.english: "The children of Israel" — to exclude what?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Looks closely at one phrase in the פסוק just quoted.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which group's קרבנות the words "בני ישראל" would seem to leave out.

steps.title: It can't exclude women
steps.stepSummary: Maybe "בני" (sons) excludes women's קרבנות. But that would mean a woman's קרבן may be offered in טומאה, which is impossible.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it comes to exclude women — can a woman's קרבן really be offered in impurity?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא suggests that "בני ישראל" leaves out women, and then rejects the idea right away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If women were excluded, the פסוק's warning would not apply to their קרבנות, and they could be brought in טומאה. That is clearly not true, so this reading fails.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say (a suggestion about to be rejected)

phrases.english: If we say it is to exclude women —
phrases.notes: The idea is that "בני" means sons, so daughters would be left out.

phrases.english: is a women's offering sacrificed in impurity?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proposes a first answer to step 13 and rejects it.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects reading "בני ישראל" as excluding women.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It would lead to the absurd result that women's קרבנות may be offered in טומאה.

steps.title: It can't exclude gentiles either
steps.stepSummary: Maybe it excludes גוים. But even the ציץ does not help a גוי's קרבן that was offered in טומאה, so it surely cannot be offered in טומאה from the start.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it excludes gentiles? But the ציץ doesn't even make their קרבן accepted, as the Master said: for gentiles, whether by mistake or on purpose, it was not accepted. So can it be offered in impurity?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries a second answer, that "בני ישראל" leaves out גוים, and rejects it with a קל וחומר. This leaves the question open for the real answer, which comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For a Jew's קרבן offered in טומאה, the כהן גדול's ציץ can make it accepted after the fact. For a גוי's קרבן, it does not help at all. If a גוי's קרבן is weaker even after the fact, it certainly may not be offered in טומאה to begin with. So excluding גוים makes no sense either.

keyTerms.meaning: The gold frontplate worn by the כהן גדול

steps.whatToRemember: "בני ישראל" cannot be excluding women or גוים, because neither group's קרבנות may be offered in טומאה. So the words must mean something else, and that is how the גמרא will find the source for זר.

phrases.english: Rather, it is to exclude gentiles?
Now, if the frontplate does not effect acceptance for them,
phrases.notes: Normally the ציץ makes a Jew's קרבן accepted even if it was offered in טומאה.

phrases.english: as the Master said:
And with gentiles — whether unintentionally or intentionally,
it was not accepted;
can it then be sacrificed in impurity?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries a second answer after step 14 failed, and rejects it as well.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects reading "בני ישראל" as excluding גוים.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A קל וחומר: the ציץ does not even help a גוי's קרבן after the fact, so it certainly cannot be offered in טומאה from the start.

steps.title: Re-reading the פסוק with a new pause
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers its question by moving the break in the פסוק. 'בני ישראל' is not tied to 'the holy things'. It starts the next phrase: 'בני ישראל shall not profane.' This teaches that a זר who serves profanes the עבודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, this is what the פסוק means: 'Let them [the כהנים] separate from the holy things. The children of Israel shall not profane.'
steps.whatsHappening: Both attempts to explain what 'בני ישראל' leaves out failed. So the גמרא changes how the פסוק is divided, and the problem goes away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before, 'בני ישראל' was read as 'the holy things of בני ישראל', which seemed to leave something out. Now the first half tells the כהנים to separate from קדשים, and the second half is a command about ordinary Jews: they must not profane the עבודה. That second half is the source that a זר makes the עבודה פסול.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, this is what it is saying. Used to offer a new reading of a text.

steps.confusionAlert: Don't read 'בני ישראל' together with 'the holy things'. The whole point of the answer is that 'בני ישראל' belongs to the words after it: 'בני ישראל shall not profane.'
steps.whyThisMatters: This new reading turns a phrase that seemed to limit the law into the actual source for the rule that a זר disqualifies the עבודה.

steps.title: A second source: קל וחומר from a blemished כהן
steps.stepSummary: The school of רבי ישמעאל learns the law of a זר through a קל וחומר from a כהן בעל מום. A בעל מום may eat קדשים, yet if he serves, he profanes the עבודה. The argument continues in the next section.
steps.simpleTranslation: The school of רבי ישמעאל taught: it comes through a קל וחומר from a blemished כהן. A בעל מום is allowed to eat, yet if he served, he profaned the עבודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a different way to prove that a זר disqualifies the עבודה. This line only sets up the first half of the קל וחומר, and the conclusion comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A כהן with a blemish is still a כהן and may eat קדשים, yet his עבודה is still profaned. The setup suggests a stronger point is coming: a זר may not even eat קדשים, so his עבודה should surely be profaned.

keyTerms.meaning: The school of רבי ישמעאל taught

phrases.english: The school of Rabbi Yishmael taught:
It is derived through an a fortiori argument from a blemished priest:

if he performed the service, he profaned it;
